name: EndeavorRx
one_liner: Prescription video-game treatment for children 8–17 with inattentive or combined-type ADHD, used alongside other ADHD care.
best_for: Parents of children 8–17 with inattentive or combined-type ADHD, working with their child's doctor
Families wanting a non-drug option to add alongside medication or behavioural therapy
not_for: Adults 18 and over (the separate EndeavorOTC app is for adults)
Children under 8, or children with ADHD of the hyperactive-impulsive type only
Anyone looking for a replacement for medication, therapy or school support
Anyone in crisis or thinking about suicide: call or text 988
short_description: FDA-authorized prescription video game for children 8–17 with inattentive or combined-type ADHD. Needs a prescription; adults use EndeavorOTC.
long_description: EndeavorRx (AKL-T01), made by Akili, is a prescription digital therapeutic for children aged 8 to 17 with primarily inattentive or combined-type ADHD who have a demonstrated attention issue. The child steers a character through courses while responding to targets and ignoring distractions; the game adapts difficulty as they play. The FDA authorized it in June 2020 through the De Novo pathway (DEN200026), based mainly on the STARS-ADHD randomized trial of 348 children, which found a small improvement on a computerised attention test versus a control game; it is not a stand-alone treatment for ADHD. It needs a prescription and is dispensed through a pharmacy; the free demo has no therapeutic effect. Akili was acquired by Virtual Therapeutics in 2024. Adults 18 and older can use the separate non-prescription EndeavorOTC.
patient_summary: EndeavorRx is a prescription treatment for children aged 8 to 17 with ADHD: a doctor prescribes it and your child plays a game on a phone or tablet for about 25 minutes a day, about five days a week. It aims to improve attention and is meant to be used with other treatment, such as medication or behavioural therapy, not instead of it. It is filled through a pharmacy; insurance coverage varies.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; about $592 cash per prescription (pharmacy list price)
pricing.notes: Filled through a pharmacy with a prescription. SingleCare lists an average retail price of about $592.51, or about $442 with its coupon. Insurance coverage is inconsistent. The free demo is for look and feel only. Adults use EndeavorOTC, sold separately ($69.99 for 3 months to $129.99 for 12 months).

privacy.notes: Akili's notice says data is used only to provide the app, support users and coordinate treatment with the prescriber or pharmacy; marketing is opt-in; deletion by email request. HIPAA status not stated.

seo.title: EndeavorRx: FDA-Approved Video Game for ADHD | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: EndeavorRx is the first FDA-approved prescription video game for pediatric ADHD. Improves attention in children ages 8-17 through engaging game-based therapy.

faqs.a: EndeavorRx is the first FDA-approved prescription treatment delivered through a video game, designed for children ages 8-17 with inattentive or combined-type ADHD to improve attention function.

The game uses sensory stimuli and motor challenges to target brain areas key to attention. Kids navigate courses, collect targets, and avoid obstacles while being challenged to multitask and ignore distractions.

faqs.q: What is the EndeavorRx treatment protocol?
faqs.a: Children play for 25 minutes per day, 5 days per week, for 4 weeks. Clinical trials showed roughly half of parents reported clinically meaningful improvement after one month.

faqs.q: What ages is EndeavorRx approved for?
faqs.a: EndeavorRx was initially approved for ages 8-12 and has been expanded by the FDA to include adolescents ages 13-17 with ADHD.

primary_uses: Prescription attention treatment for children with ADHD
Add-on to medication or behavioural therapy
Improving sustained attention on objective testing
